function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL to retrieve weather data from the Open-Meteo API. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: URL of the Open-Meteo API endpoint.

headers.description: Headers to include in the request. Each key-value pair represents a header field and its value.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

timeout.description: Maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters for the GET request.

latitude.description: Latitude of the location, positive for N and negative for S. This is a float type value.

longitude.description: Longitude of the location, positive for E and negative for W. This is a float type value.

elevation.description: Elevation in meters above sea level for the location. The default value represents no elevation downscaling.

auth.description: Authentication tuple for HTTP authentication, in the format (username, password).

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem). A null value means no client certificate is used.

cookies.description: Dictionary of cookies to send with the request. Each key represents a cookie name.

proxies.description: Dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy. Each key-value pair represents a protocol and its proxy URL.

stream.description: If True, the response should be streamed; otherwise, it should be downloaded immediately.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate.

**Park Ji‑sung** (박지성) – commonly known as **Ji‑sung Park** in Western contexts – is a retired South‑Korean professional footballer who is widely regarded as one of the most successful Asian players in European football history.

| Category | Details |
|----------|---------|
| **Full name** | Park Ji‑sung (박지성) |
| **Date of birth** | 25 March 1981 |
| **Place of birth** | Seoul, South Korea |
| **Position** | Midfielder (primarily a box‑to‑box, defensive midfielder) |
| **Height** | 1.78 m (5 ft 10 in) |

### Club Career Highlights

| Years | Club | Appearances | Goals |
|-------|------|-------------|-------|
| 1999–2000 | Suwon Samsung Bluewings (K League) | 30 | 4 |
| 2000–2001 | PSV Eindhoven (Eredivisie) | 55 | 7 |
| 2001–2015 | Manchester United (Premier League) | 423 | 23 |
| 2015–2016 | PSV Eindhoven (Eredivisie) | 27 | 1 |
| 2016–2017 | FC Seoul (K League) | 12 | 0 |

- **Manchester United**: 14‑year tenure, 423 league appearances, 23 goals. Won 5 Premier League titles, 1 FA Cup, 1 League Cup, 1 UEFA Champions League (2008), 1 UEFA Europa League (2016), and 1 FIFA Club World Cup (2008).
- **PSV Eindhoven**: Key role in the club’s 2000–01 Eredivisie title and 2001 UEFA Cup win.
- **Suwon Samsung Bluewings**: Early career success, winning the K League title in 2000.

### International Career

- **South Korea National Team**: 2000–2016, 120 caps, 6 goals.
- **World Cups**: 2002 (co‑hosted by South Korea/Japan – reached semi‑finals), 2006, 2010, 2014.
- **Asian Cup**: 2000, 2004, 2010 (runner‑up in 2010).
- **Olympics**: 2004 Athens (bronze medal).

### Notable Achievements & Records

- First Asian player to win the Premier League, FA Cup, and UEFA Champions League with the same club.
- Holds the record for the most Premier League appearances by an Asian player (423).
- Known for his stamina, work‑rate, and tactical intelligence—often described as the “engine” of the midfield.
- Awarded the **Korean Footballer of the Year** multiple times (2002, 2003, 2004, 2005, 2006, 2007, 2008, 2009, 2010, 2011, 2012, 2013, 2014, 2015, 2016).

### Post‑Retirement

- **Coaching**: Served as a coach for the South Korean national team’s U‑23 squad and later as an assistant coach for the senior national team.
- **Media & Commentary**: Regular football analyst on Korean sports networks.
- **Philanthropy**: Involved in various charitable initiatives, including youth football development programs in South Korea.

### Personal Life

- Married to Kim Hye‑jin (former Miss Korea) in 2014; they have two children.
- Known for his humility and professionalism both on and off the pitch.

---

#### Quick Facts

- **Nickname**: “The Engine” (due to his relentless energy).
- **Preferred Foot**: Right.
- **Playing Style**: Box‑to‑box midfielder, excellent passing range, strong tackling, and a knack for scoring crucial goals.

---

**Other Individuals Named Park Ji‑sung**

While Park Ji‑sung the footballer is the most internationally recognized, there are other Korean personalities with the same name, such as:

- **Park Ji‑sung (actor)** – born 1979, known for roles in Korean dramas like *“The King’s Face”* and *“The Great Seer.”*
- **Park Ji‑sung (musician)** – a lesser‑known singer-songwriter active in the indie scene.

If you were referring to a different Ji‑sung Park, let me know and I can provide more specific information!
